subject: PO requirements & invoice timing for Novaris Health
messages:
From: Sarah Gupta <sarah.gupta@novarishealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PO requirements & invoice timing for Novaris Health

Hi Chloe / Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — procurement asked me to put the PO details in writing so we can move to contract and payment setup. A few specific asks from our AP/process team:

- PO identifier must be present on every invoice in "PO#" field and in the invoice PDF header.
- We operate a weekly billing sweep (Friday 23:59 ET). Invoices received after the Friday cutoff are paid on the following week's run.
- Net terms: standard is Net 45 but we can discuss Net 30 for the first 90 days if required.
- We prefer monthly consolidated invoices when multiple POs are active, but Novaris will accept weekly if the PO includes a line for "usage summary" per week.

I attached our PO template (Novaris_PO_template_2026-02-10.xlsx). Can Redwood accept the PO identifier enforcement and provide sample invoice PDF showing the PO in the header? Also please confirm whether Redwood can support a pre-bill holdback (Novaris may hold 5% for 30 days on first invoices for new vendors).

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is targeting a 2/24 activation if we can confirm formatting and net terms.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Gupta
Procurement Lead, Novaris Health

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PO requirements & invoice timing for Novaris Health

Hi Sarah — thanks for sharing the template and the clear asks. Short answers up front:

- PO identifier on invoice header: yes, we can include a dedicated PO# field on the PDF and metadata so your ERP can parse it.
- Weekly billing sweep: we can schedule invoice submission to your preferred cutoffs. We typically push invoices as soon as usage closes; we can batch to align with Fri 23:59 ET.
- Net terms: standard Redwood terms are Net 30 for new enterprise customers, but we can scope Net 45 for the committed term if necessary. We can also offer a Net 30 pilot period — happy to confirm which you prefer.
- Pre-bill holdback: we can add a 5% line item flagged as "holdback" on the first invoice; however, we need to align on accounting reconciliation steps so it doesn't break automated recognition in our finance system.

I'll loop in Karthik from finance to confirm the exact invoice file layout (CSV + PDF) and whether the holdback has to be a separate credit memo or may be encoded as a flagged line on the initial invoice. Vanessa — can you confirm whether Sales/CS needs to mirror anything in the contract language for holdbacks?

Next steps proposal:
1) Redwood to send a sample invoice PDF + CSV that includes the PO header and a flagged holdback line (by EOD 2/11).
2) Novaris to confirm acceptance of file layout and whether consolidated monthly vs weekly is required at go-live.
3) Finalize net terms (Net 30 vs Net 45) and reflect in SOW/PO by 2/17 to keep the 2/24 activation target.

Thanks — Chloe

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: PO requirements & invoice timing for Novaris Health

Chloe / Karthik — forwarding Sarah's template and Chloe's note. Karthik, two quick clarifications for finance:

1) If Novaris holds 5% on first invoice, do we (a) issue the invoice with a 5% line flagged as "holdback" and reconcile when released, or (b) issue full invoice and expect a separate credit memo? Either is workable, but ERP mapping differs.

2) For weekly versus monthly consolidation: our billing system can emit both weekly CSVs and a monthly roll-up PDF. If Novaris wants weekly sweeps, we need to ensure we can label lines by PO and week (week-of YYYY-MM-DD) so their AP can auto-match.

I reviewed the sample Redwood-invoice-sample.pdf Chloe attached — good start, but we need to add a visible PO# in the page header and expose PO metadata in the CSV header row as PO_ID. Karthik — can you confirm the CSV header we should land on? I suggest: invoice_id, invoice_date, po_id, line_description, usage_start, usage_end, quantity, unit_price, line_total, holdback_flag.

Karthik — please confirm and advise on how the holdback should be processed on your side (credit memo vs flagged line).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Success Operations

Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: PO requirements & invoice timing for Novaris Health

Vanessa / Chloe — thanks. Confirming finance stance:

- Preferred approach: issue initial invoice with the full billed amount and include a separate credit note when the 5% holdback is released. Reason: many ERPs ingest credit memos better than flagged partial payments. However, we can also emit the invoice with a "holdback_flag" field — we will need a matching credit memo or negative invoice to clear the holdback in our ledger. Either approach is fine; recommend the credit memo path to keep audit trail clean.

- CSV header: Karthik confirms the suggested header looks good. Slight tweak: include a "po_line_ref" column for multi-line POs and a "currency" column. Final header example: invoice_id, invoice_date, po_id, po_line_ref, line_description, usage_start, usage_end, quantity, unit_price, line_total, currency, holdback_flag.

- For weekly sweeps: we can produce weekly CSVs labelled by week-of and a monthly consolidated PDF. If Novaris chooses weekly, we will also provide a monthly consolidated file for month-end reconciliation.

I'll draft a short spec and send by EOD 2/11.

Karthik
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
